scope: Import source material -> generate a local draft -> strict independent evidence verification -> explicit manual acceptance
excludedScope: External connector synchronization and identity-bound subprocess lifecycle
External publication and end-to-end external delivery
Historical Agent authorization-repair and autonomous continuation

review.reviewer: Independent source-and-artifact reviewer; retrospective nonblind audit

conditions.requirement: Install or distribute the reviewed package identity. Any executable/product-code or ASAR change needs fresh identity and affected-scope verification; documentary-only packaging changes need an updated archive hash.

At installation, read back strict evidence grounding enabled, automatic management disabled and automatic completion disabled. Use one explicitly advanced local draft task at a time and require human review before acceptance.

Do not activate or represent external connector synchronization, external publication, complete Agent delegation or historical Agent recovery as certified behavior of this delivery. Existing automatic/external work must not be resumed as part of installation.
Publish the original full-run and fixed-rerun totals and these four unpassed cases alongside the limited-scope delivery statement. Never describe this delivery as globally green.
This approval authorizes no new model calls, health probes or reuse of the halted evaluation budget.

review.conclusion: No necessary P0/P1 product repair was identified within the foundation scope fixed before testing. The exact historical-J package may be installed and delivered under the listed operating and disclosure conditions. Global regression and the fixed targeted rerun remain failed; the four residual cases remain visible and do not become passed through this scoped approval.

verification.originalWriteResponseLostAssertion: failed in full run; passed in the original-condition fixed rerun; original failure retained

residualFailures.test: Codex subprocess activity extends idle window without a total deadline
residualFailures.scopeAssessment: This test starts the managed Windows process with a 200 ms idle window. The unchanged production policy defaults to 900000 ms and accepts whole-minute user settings. Three offline observations of the same managed spawn path first emitted stdout after 217.7025, 240.9237 and 226.3692 ms. This supports a fixture startup-budget explanation; the diagnostic is not an acceptance pass and uses an inherited environment rather than processCall’s filtered environment.
residualFailures.disposition: Retain the failing test and diagnostic. No production waiting-policy change or further retest is required for the declared foundation delivery.

residualFailures.test: I13 actual same-group descendant ignores TERM; abort-transient-probe waits for group exit before session cleanup
residualFailures.scopeAssessment: The failing wait at line 117 precedes the transient-confirmation probe injection. It waits for a synthetic Lark connector descendant readiness marker and process-group record after identity binding and connector sync. Close and ordinary abort variants passed the fixed rerun; the transient-probe scenario remains unverified. The certified workflow neither synchronizes this connector nor invokes its identity-bound process session.
residualFailures.disposition: Keep as an unresolved external-connector limitation. Do not claim that the transient probe, descendant cleanup or the whole connector lifecycle passed.

residualFailures.scopeAssessment: The test sets automaticExecution=true and runs agent.run on a delegation whose contract reads 19 sources, revises an existing main artifact and updates the same external Lark document with readback. It exercises a broader automatic Agent contract than the declared local manual task path. The actual foundation renderer/IPC/Worker generate-check-accept-persist route passed on the same ASAR; this does not validate the failed complete Agent route.
residualFailures.disposition: Do not certify complete Agent check-revise or external publication. Retain this timeout without attributing it to environment.

residualFailures.test: controlled/notproduction formal Worker: context authorization repair uses normal RPC across upgrade and committed-repair cold restarts
residualFailures.scopeAssessment: The same external-delivery delegation is seeded with a historical context failure, 20 synthetic billed requests and a permission decision. The test repairs it using agentCheckResume and normal Worker resume RPC across restarts. A read-only observation helper times out after 15000 ms; the log does not locate the underlying product or fixture cause. This historical automatic-delegation recovery path is outside the predeclared foundation contract.
residualFailures.disposition: Do not certify historical Agent authorization repair or full recovery. Preserve the unresolved timeout.

limitations: This is a scoped delivery decision, not a blanket assertion of software correctness. Four original-condition rerun cases remain unpassed.
The three connector/Agent failures have unresolved causes. Their exclusion follows the scope fixed before results, not a claim that environment caused them.
The subsecond timing diagnosis supports an explanation for that fixture failure but does not rerun or pass the original test and does not prove future online service behavior.
The two source-to-draft smoke runs used loopback synthetic responses. The IPC accept command was automated; a real human reading and approving a real model draft was not measured.
Foundation v2 registered pageerror on all three main windows; the earlier Windows smoke only observed its first main window. Neither result guarantees every possible renderer condition.
Historical J review is retrospective and nonblind, and its generated sample size is four per arm. It is not a population-level no-hallucination claim.
The reviewer performed no live calls, network probes, installation, product edits or credential-file reads.
